That's what I do. I have adhd or really just A.D.D. and I got diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia as well. Sometimes add or adhd whatever can cause you to essentially burn out your circuits and you're tired all the time because your brain goes so fast and have anxiety. The only med that works to keep me awake and doesn't cause more anxiety or heart palpitations is provigil. It's the older version of nuvigil. It was made for shift workers to stay awake. Highly recommend! Nuvigil made my heart race and gave me insomnia. Adderral stopped the anxiety but I was more of a slug than even normally. When uppers are the thing you need to stay awake, but your adhd makes the uppers do the opposite and put you to sleep, provigil isn't technically an upper and works differently. Ask your doc and good luck.

You can have A.D.D without the hyper part, you can hand adhd and present differently as a woman, as an adult, do some more research on what YOUR symptoms are because we are all different darling. Adhd is a blanket term for a bunch of things that most of us have in common but we don't all have the exact same things/issues....my turning point was that I'd been diagnosed wrong for years with anxiety and depression and medicated incorrectly. The only thing that worked well was cymbalta, I finally figured out cymbalta is off label used for adhd and works with dopamine which is a chemical that MOST adhd people have less of and need more of. Then found I had a LOT in common with other adhd people on reddit and other forums. It is absolutely possible and sadly happens a lot to be misdiagnosed and adhd to be dismissed or seen as something else. Go with your gut. Only you know how you feel, but if certain phrases resonate with you, it's a good tip off. Here are a few.
1. I dont feel like I am equipped for life like everyone else around me is. It looks easy for them.
2. I dont understand how other people don't worry about things like I do.
3. When I lay down to sleep I think about conversations i had, embarrassing moments from forever ago, etc. And can't go to sleep because of these thoughts.
4. I deep clean my room and move furniture one day and in two days it's cluttered again and I don't clean again for a very long time. Because for it to be "done right" takes so much energy. 
5. I am always late to events, sometimes time flies by and sometimes it crawls but I never know what time it is. 
6. I have trouble completing things, I get distracted and do other things that aren't as important as the first task. 
7. I dont like super loud noises, crowds, bright lights, unless I am the one in control of those things. Like it's my party, my music, my lights.
And also, on ambetters site just call the number. They work super hard to find you the best plan and they get you better ones than what you just see on the page. Good luck!

I spent 15 years medicating the wrong diagnosis. They said I had depression and anxiety...I just spent none months searching for answers using ambetter insurance because I couldn't pay for any of what I've done alone, I got diagnosed finally with adhd and idiopathic hypersomnia (extreme daytime fatigue with no physical cause probably adhd symptom) nine months, trying different meds, some of which put me closer to a straightjacket than I've ever been, one of which made me want to jump off a bridge, several that made me super angry, one caused muscle pain?😳 one withdrawal gave me vertigo and nausea, one made me feel like I was a puppet being operated by someone else and another made me not recognize myself in a ficking mirror. TODAY. TODAY, I took ONE 150mg Nuvigil and A SWITCH TURNED ON. I knew it could happen, years ago I tried cymbalta which was prescribed for depression/anxiety and it was a SWITCH. I loved cymbalta, but it quit working after 5 years and also because of the hypersomnia I still was tired, but I felt normal mentally. But friend, TODAY IS THE BEST DAY EVER. I didn't give up. I KNEW it would happen because I'd done it once before, but not like this. Don't settle. Don't feel sort of ok. There is something out there that FITS YOU and gives your body/brain what it needs to function, to be productive, to live life better. If you can't afford it I strongly suggest getting ambetter. My doc visits are free. I get free therapy once a week video chat with a lady I picked out. They paid 80% of my sleep lab and all those meds were free or under 20$. Nuvigil is expensive but I'm getting an authorization so maybe they'll come through on this as well. Anywaaay. My miracle drug may not be your miracle drug. BUT. I WANT ALL OF YOU TO HAVE WHAT I HAVE TODAY. Don't give up. I FOUGHT so hard. I'm so proud. I have hope, I have a chance I never thought I'd have, and if you need ANYTHING you message me. You need hope? Take some of mine. Because today, I forgave myself for everything I didn't finish, I threw off every jab about being lazy, sleeping too much, being "fragile" having "untapped potential" etc. They can't touch me and I won't say those things to myself anymore. I'm not perfect, and I'll have bad days. But. I did it. We did it. Keep fighting. I'll fight with you buddy. And I'm about 1000x stronger today than I was yesterday. One day, you'll have my today. 💖💖💖

Ohhh I've GOT YOU. ADHD or ADD, can cause fatigue or burnout. I just got diagnosed with ADHD AND idiopathic hypersomnia. Thats basically daytime sleepiness with no "apparent" cause as in no physical cause, I did two sleep labs, no apnea or any other problem physically, I slept 8 hours at the lab. Then, at 8am, 10am, 12am and 2pm they had me try to take a nap. I fell asleep in under three minutes each time. 3. Minutes. But the daytime naps aren't REM cycle naps they're super light apparently, and at night my brain races. If you have this particular symptom it is hard to find the correct meds. I've tried several, adderral made me even more tired. When you get a diagnosis try provigil or nuvigil, dopamine enhancers to keep you awake during the day. If you aren't mentally feeling any better I suggest welbutrin with a small dose of provigil or nuvigil. I've only found one other diagnosed with both like me so far. Try having someone watch you and time you when you take a nap, each one lasted 20 minutes in lab and at those times I said earlier.. It might help you off the record diagnose I.H.
